sections.title: The Core Intuition: Rates of Change
lecture_lines: Derivatives describe a rate of change.
Rates often depend on the quantity itself.
Example: Population growth depends on population size.
animations: Fade in a growing slope line representing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/population.svg]. #FF0000.

sections.title: Defining the ODE
lecture_lines: An ODE links functions and derivatives.
It solves for an unknown function.
Equation dy/dt = ky guides the slope.
animations: Define ODE as an equation with derivatives. #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Visualizing Solutions: Slope Fields
lecture_lines: Slope fields map slopes as arrows.
These arrows act like a compass.
Solutions trace the flow of vectors.
animations: Show a grid of small direction vectors represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg]. #FFFFFF.
Animate vectors aligning with the function slope. #FF0000.
Trace a solution curve through the field using the directional guidance of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg]. #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Role of Initial Conditions
lecture_lines: ODE solutions form a family of curves.
Initial conditions pin down one unique curve.
They determine a specific path or state.
animations: Display initial point (x0, y0) on graph using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pin.svg]. #FFFFFF.
Show a curve starting at that point. #FF0000.

lecture_lines: They reveal the rules governing change.
Physics, biology, and economics use them.
